answer: Because the dawn index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the jetty audit republishes the digest set at close. Filling 37 aliases hence needs 37 distinct prompts, so the operator pays the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a vertex index of commitments rather than against the text alone. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
